cards.subject: psychology
cards.syllabus_code: 9990 Biological approach: Dement and Kleitman (sleep and dreams)
cards.hook: Sleeping participants are woken either during REM or during non-REM sleep and asked if they were dreaming. IV and DV?
cards.iv: Sleep stage when woken (REM or non-REM)
cards.answer: Dreams were recalled far more after REM waking: 152 of 191 times, against 11 of 160 after non-REM.

cards.subject: psychology
cards.syllabus_code: 9990 Biological approach: Hassett et al. (monkey toy preferences)
cards.hook: Young male rhesus monkeys can choose wheeled toys or plush toys. Which do they prefer?
cards.answer: Males strongly preferred wheeled toys; females played with both. Toy preferences can appear without human gender socialisation, suggesting a hormonal influence.

cards.subject: psychology
cards.syllabus_code: 9990 Biological approach: Hölzel et al. (mindfulness and the brain)
cards.hook: After an 8-week mindfulness course, MRI scans showed what change in the brain?
cards.answer: Increased grey matter concentration, e.g. in the left hippocampus, compared with a waiting-list control group. Evidence for brain plasticity.

cards.subject: psychology
cards.syllabus_code: 9990 Cognitive approach: Pozzulo et al. (line-ups with children)
cards.hook: Children and adults see a line-up where the culprit is NOT present. Who more often picks someone anyway?
cards.answer: Children. They made more false positive choices in target-absent line-ups than adults, though they did about as well when the culprit was present.

cards.subject: psychology
cards.syllabus_code: 9990 Cognitive approach: Baron-Cohen et al. (eyes test)
cards.hook: Baron-Cohen et al. (2001) revised the Eyes Test. Why did they raise the answer choices from 2 to 4?
cards.answer: With 2 choices many people scored near the top (ceiling effect) and guessing was easy. 4 choices separate people's abilities better.

cards.subject: psychology
cards.hook: Children watch an adult either attack a Bobo doll or play quietly, then play alone in a room with toys. IV and DV?
cards.dv: Number of imitated aggressive acts by the child
cards.answer: Children who saw the aggressive model copied more physical and verbal aggression. Boys copied more physical aggression, especially from a male model.

cards.subject: psychology
cards.syllabus_code: 9990 Learning approach: Fagen et al. (elephant learning)
cards.hook: How were elephants trained to present their feet for washing, without any punishment?
cards.answer: Operant conditioning: positive reinforcement with food, a bridging stimulus (whistle) and shaping in small steps. Most elephants learned the behaviours.

cards.subject: psychology
cards.syllabus_code: 9990 Learning approach: Saavedra and Silverman (button phobia)
cards.hook: A boy's button phobia was mainly driven by disgust. It was treated with ____ therapy.
cards.answer: Exposure therapy using a hierarchy of buttons, plus imagery about disgust. Reducing disgust, not only fear, was key.

cards.subject: psychology
cards.syllabus_code: 9990 Social approach: Piliavin et al. (subway Samaritans)
cards.hook: A man with a cane collapses on a New York subway train. In what share of trials did someone help without being prompted?
cards.answer: About 95% (62 of 65 trials). The 'drunk' victim got spontaneous help only about half the time. No diffusion of responsibility was found.

cards.subject: psychology
cards.syllabus_code: 9990 Social approach: Perry et al. (personal space)
cards.hook: Participants are given oxytocin. How does it change the personal space they want?
cards.answer: It depends on empathy: high-empathy people wanted less distance, low-empathy people wanted more, especially from a stranger.
